core_obligations: Use that an immersion of algebraic spaces is representable to reduce to the schemes situation.
Transport the identification of the universal first order thickening and of its conormal sheaf back to the algebraic-spaces setting.

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to the schemes case using representability of the immersion.
Identify the universal first order thickening with the complement of the infinitesimal neighbourhood.
Transport the conormal sheaf identification back.

difficulty_reason: The lemma describes the universal first order thickening of an immersion of algebraic spaces: it is identified with the complement of the first order infinitesimal neighbourhood, and the conormal sheaf of the universal thickening is identified accordingly. The proof works with the definition of an immersion of algebraic spaces as a representable morphism, reduces to the schemes statement through that description, and transports the identification of the universal thickening from the schemes case. The reduction through representability is the load-bearing step. Retained author proof at lines 3166-3200 with the surrounding argument.

dedup.scope: Cross-chapter same-name pair decided by the statements alone: both sides identify the universal first order thickening of an immersion with the complement of the infinitesimal neighbourhood. This side states it for algebraic spaces over S and carries the genuine 13-line proof, so it is the side counted. Compared against all focused-seeds task.json, PREPARATION_WORKLIST.jsonl, and public intervals for spaces-more-morphisms.tex.

compared.difference: Hypothesis difference: the schemes side assumes an immersion of schemes; this side an immersion of algebraic spaces over S. Conclusion difference: none, both identify the universal thickening and its conormal sheaf.
